_about: Appendix D of the suite results document, the glossary (round 2, after OWNER-REVIEW-SAMPLE-1.md; the readability review of the full v4 report, READ-020, READ-022, READ-024, 2026-10-15): `entries` is a list of {term, definition, see} (see: other terms, optional); the generator prints them in alphabetical order in two columns at footnote size, over two pages where they need them (no longer forced onto one page). Each entry is a plain definition and one consequence; the policy detail is left to the appendix the entry names. The core outcome terms read the shared vocabulary (doc/vocabulary.py) through the `vocab[...]` placeholders, the same texts the reading guide's legend and appendix F's tables print, so that the three cannot drift. A term of a later manifest version is labelled as not exercised by a run of another version through a conditional on `manifest_version`. The long form (every term of the suite) is the glossary section of the suite's README (`readme`: path and section; `commit` pins it by hand, else the generator reads the commit that last touched the README in the checkout); `lead` is printed above the entries with that pin. `records_key.lead` heads the record key the generator prints before the entries from the manifest's ground_truth.records. Definitions follow the suite's README, checks.py, compare.py, report.py and gate.py as of c11db9dd, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 4 and SPEC-pattern-search sections 7 and 9. Inline markup: `code` and *emphasis*; placeholders as in overview.json. The entry on the stated stop states whether the run answered one through the run-wide placeholders resolve_stop_observed and resolve_stop_ids (facts.resolve_stops: every /resolve scenario, every arm), never as a fixed sentence (the v5 merge, 2026-10-15).

_assumes._note: The literal numbers this file's prose may carry, each with its source: constants of the SPEC, of the manifest v4 (lengths, budgets, expected runs), of the service's table or of the harness, never a figure of a run (those are placeholders the generator fills). tests/test_doc.py fails on a number the prose carries that is listed neither here nor as a placeholder; add a constant here with its source, never a run's figure.
_assumes.0: repeat 0 (the harness); runs 0-based (SPEC section 4.1); an exact count of 0 (SPEC-pattern-search section 9)
_assumes.1: L - k + 1 (SPEC section 4.1); max(1 s, the budget) (checks.py)
_assumes.2: the sampler's 2 s interval (sampler.py); DUST below 2 (areas.py)
_assumes.100: 100 % of docker stats' CPU is one logical CPU (docker stats); a 100 bp query (the worked example of the run's unit, SPEC section 4.1)
_assumes.250: the finalisation reserve in ms (SPEC section 4.5)
_assumes.31: k, the index's k-mer length (manifest index.k)
_assumes.70: the k-mer starts of a 100 bp query at k = 31, L - k + 1 (SPEC section 4.1)

readme.pin: the checks commit and the manifest version named on the title page and in I.4; the README section states the commit it was written for

lead: The terms a reader needs to interpret the evidence, each a plain definition and one consequence; the long form of every term of the suite is the glossary section of `{readme_path}` as of commit {readme_commit}, pinned to the checks and the manifest version this document names, so that an archived report stays interpretable. The outcome terms are the shared definitions of the reading guide (I.3) and appendix F. The record key precedes the entries; the matrices' legends link to it.

entries.definition: One frozen test of the manifest: an id (family prefix and number, e.g. R-pos-0013), a route, the exact request, the ground truth, the expectations (check and arguments), the MCP mapping, a timing class, a repeat count, tags. The tables' test id is the scenario id; a scenario count counts tests, never executions.

One request of one scenario on one access path: status, wall and server times, host-cache state, checks, outcome. Repeat 0 is the path's first; an MCP scenario the service can express has two (cold, then warm), every tenth scenario and chapter D have direct repeats. An execution count counts requests, so it exceeds the scenario count (I.4 defines the counting units).

A chapter is an area (R resolve, T traverse, P and L patterns, X peptides, M mismatches, Q predicates, C capabilities, N negatives, D determinism); a family the scenarios sharing an id prefix; a unit one builder template, one property, varied over one dimension, printed as one table. Appendix E maps every id to its unit's page.
{vocab[access_path]} direct-local is the reference path of the MCP comparison.

One of the two directions a /traverse walk extends a seed in: right (the successors of the seed's last node) or left (the predecessors of its first); a request names one or both. A per-arm cap of a walk is a cap per direction, never per access path.

A k-mer is k = {k} bases, a node of this basic graph (forward strand only: a k-mer and its reverse complement are different nodes); a query of L bases has L - k + 1, numbered from 0. Runs are 0-based half-open intervals of k-mer starts, not of bases: a 100 bp query at k = 31 has 70 k-mer starts, so [0, 70) is full coverage and spans the bases [0, 100); `graph_runs` the in-graph k-mers, a label's runs those it supports, `kmers_supported` their count. The coordinates of trace support (T-coords) and of chapter N's intervals are positions in the source record's bases. Support of a label at a k-mer says that some record of the label carries that k-mer, nothing about the rest of the query.

A column label is a taxid, one column of the annotation, with one or many records: it supports an in-graph k-mer whose row carries it. A header label is an accession.version, one record of a column reached through the coordinates: it supports a k-mer when a coordinate of its column at that row maps to the record; with support trace only while consecutive k-mers have consecutive coordinates (SPEC 4.2). A column's support can come from any of its records.

A context is one k-mer of the index containing the pattern at one offset and orientation (SPEC-pattern-search 7.1): not a locus of a genome and not an organism. A k-mer shared by ten records is one context, a k-mer repeated in one record one context too; so a count of contexts is neither a count of occurrences nor of records, and one organism can hold many contexts.

A label listed on a context or a path says that some record of that label carries its k-mers (label support, `label_intersection` for a path). That one record holds the whole pattern or path contiguously at a place of its sequence is the stronger claim of a placed occurrence (`record_verified`), made only where the answer's coordinates verify it. Label support alone is weaker than an occurrence, and a check that reads it claims no more.

No returned hit (an empty or shortened list, withheld or cut) is no absence: inconclusive. A proven zero is an exact count of 0 in the searched scope, or a complete list (`retrieval_complete` true) without the item. No hit in a selected record is a third claim, read from a complete list's labels or occurrences. Every absence is bounded by the graph, the query and the labels searched (SPEC-pattern-search 9), never a statement about biology.
{vocab[check_outcome]}
{vocab[execution_outcome]} The verdict and the gate read the execution outcomes; the tables show the standing (I.3).
{vocab[error]}
{vocab[finding]} The detail block quotes the rule and the overrun; appendix A's decision table for `budget_respected` names the cases.

The answer could not show the property: an allowed 503 deadline (no results), a list a stated hiding shortened, a walk a stated limit stopped first, a stop that was the property and did not happen, nothing to compare, no property field exposed via MCP, a host state. Never a pass, never a failure; where the policy requires it (a gated access path, in the selection, not removed by the policy's automatic exclusions nor declared exempt), it blocks the gate (I.1 counts those).

The request cannot be asked through the MCP tools: the manifest marks it, or a by-design case names the missing argument (support, `bounds.max_query_bp`, graph, a protocol body). [[answer_side_mark ? Or, by the manifest's scenario-level mark ({answer_side_mark_text}), the request is expressible but the MCP answer lacks every field the test's property checks read.]] The cell says not exercised, never ok; the service's own refusal, when recorded, is under the row or in appendix B. A known limit, not coverage and no evidence for the property.

The MCP path legitimately differs because the service refused before host execution, relayed the host's refusal under its own code, answered after normalising the request, or set a value the request did not name, as its table documents (appendix B). Verified when the direct answer matched the case's host side and the MCP answer its service side; else mark u. The cell establishes the documented service behaviour, not the property.

[[manifest_version >= 5 ? A mark of this run's manifest. | Not part of this run's manifest (version {manifest_version}): a mark of a later manifest version, exercised by no scenario of this run and read into none of its results; defined here so that the term is not misread where a reason or a plan names it.]] A mark of one check of a scenario (`mcp.not_implemented_checks`, `mcp.by_design_checks`): on the MCP path a marked check that reads not exposed is set aside, neither compared nor counted untested, while the rest of the scenario stays tested; a marked check that reads anything else is judged as any check. Setting a check aside changes how the comparison and the gate treat it and supplies no evidence about it on that path.

An MCP execution the service ended by its own limit before the host answered (`resolve_timeout` at its deadline for the host call, a relayed `traversal_resolve_deadline` or /pattern deadline): adjudicated inconclusive when the service's own timing shows the limit was reachable, a failure otherwise. The raw check lines are kept as the intermediate evaluation; nothing of the property was shown.
{vocab[standing]}

The direct paths per scenario: identical (same digest), same checks, timing (a time limitation alone), not comparable, disagree. mcp against the reference path, check by check: agree, not comparable, disagree; not implemented and by design apart. Depth of an agreement, judged over the MCP repeats compared (a repeat inconclusive by a host state is left out and named): fully checked (every expected property check on both paths, on every compared repeat), partial, generic checks only, a refusal. An agreement compares answers with one another and is no second proof of the property; a disagreement fails the run.

Two scenarios' answers compared on one access path: `same_answer`, `prefix_equals` (resolves of pieces of one sequence agree on their common k-mers), subset, `zero_equals_absent`; pass, fail, inconclusive (no two profiles to compare) or not exposed. A consistency check between observed answers, which can share an omission; a failed relation fails the run (appendix C).

`bounds.time_budget_ms` of a /resolve (opt-in: without it no deadline), `time_budget_ms` of a /pattern, the strategy's budget of a /traverse (per seed): lowered to the server's cap and stated in limits.clamped when lowered. A /resolve keeps 250 ms to build the answer: the work stops at the budget less the reserve; a budget not above it is refused (SPEC 4.5). A budget bounds the host's work on the request or the seed, never the caller's latency or the service's queue (the scope per route in I.2).

A /resolve 200 that stopped at its budget less the reserve and says so in its stop block (reason time, `resolved_kmers`, `query_kmers`, `resolved_bp`, `remainder_from_bp`): exactly the resolve of the first `resolved_kmers` k-mers, the prefix; the rest is resolved from `remainder_from_bp`. A stop that cannot have happened fails the checks that met it. [[resolve_stop_observed ? Observed in this run ({resolve_stop_ids}). | Not observed in this run.]]

The 503 with code deadline /resolve and /pattern answer when the answer cannot be built and written within the budget: nothing partial, no results. Where the request names a budget the SPECs allow it under load, so the suite reads it as inconclusive; it is a finding when it came more than max(1 s, the budget) after the budget on the client's clock (the suite's tolerance, not a proof of where the time went: appendix A, `budget_respected`), and a failure on a /resolve without a budget.

Wall: a direct execution from sending the request to the last byte on an established connection (connect time apart); an MCP execution the whole tool interaction. Server: the host's `timing.elapsed_ms`, in brackets; none on a refusal or 503, so a server aggregate counts fewer executions than its wall aggregate and the two are not paired. Backend: the host call as the service measured it, after be; its other phases are submit, queue, terminal lag, paging.

The median and the 90th percentile of a set of times: half of them, nine in ten of them, were at most that long. In a summary line a / b is p50 / p90 over every execution with that time, whatever its outcome; a ratio or a difference reported per scenario is computed per pair first and then summarised, never as a quotient of two medians.

A recency heuristic over all access paths, recorded per execution, not a measured cache: cold, the scenario's first execution to reach the host; warm, started within {warm_window_s} s of another ending on the host; aged, later (unknown); not reached, never seen by the host. An MCP pair is cold then warm; a direct time is warm unless marked c, a or i (warm after an interrupted execution, left out of aggregates). A cold-warm difference is the difference of two executions in the loop's order, not a measured cache effect.

The nginx reverse proxy behind the public URL; every access path but direct-local goes through it. Front cost: direct-remote minus direct-local on host-warm pairs, net of the server time. Connect time: the set-up of a fresh connection (TCP, TLS), recorded apart from the wall.

docker stats of the staging and `sra_all` (Logan indexing, concurrent work on the same host) containers and the host load average, sampled every 2 s on mex and joined to each execution: the shared host's context, not any request's cost (a container CPU of 100 % is one logical CPU busy; its memory is the container's memory usage as docker stats reports it, not one query's use). The caveat is stated when the `sra_all` CPU mean exceeds {load_caveat_sra_cpu_pct} % or the load1 mean {load_caveat_load1}: such timings are not the baseline.

The run's word, in this order: INCOMPLETE (an access path unfinished, a planned execution unrecorded), FAIL (a failed or errored execution, a disagreement, a failed relation), FINDINGS, INCONCLUSIVE (nothing passed, a group tested nothing, two deployments), PASS; EMPTY and UNVERIFIED (a status-only stub). Inconclusive executions are counted after it, never as passes; beside a gate the verdict is exploratory.

The release decision: a strict judgement of the run's records against a policy that pins the manifest, relations, index and by-design table, selects scenarios by route and names the gated access paths; it fails on anything missing, any non-pass on a gated path, any mark it cannot explain, any disagreement, any required relation not passed, configuration evidence not recorded live (the rules and the problems by group in appendix F). The declared file is the owner's reasoned exemptions: they change what the gate requires, not what the run observed (appendix G).

A test is clean when every access path is a pass, not exercised via MCP, a by-design pair (verified, or unverified with the mark u, whose cause the chapter's prose and appendix B state), or had no planned execution: it carries no detail block. Clean means no exception to explain, not that every property was shown through every path. Any other test carries a footnote digit on its offending cells and a detail block after its table (numbering restarts per chapter), which opens with what was requested, observed and left unverified.

One indexed sequence of the ground truth, named by its accession.version (header label), in a taxid column (column label): the {n_records} genomes of the search service's validation set, fetched at the indexed version. A window is a stretch of a record's forward strand cut at a seeded position (ACGT only, DUST below 2, unique on either strand). The tables use the keys above.

records_key.lead: The record abbreviations of the matrices (the manifest's ground truth; the accession.version is the record's header label, the taxid its column label):
records_key.source: the manifest's ground_truth.records (key, label, accession, taxid, kingdom, length, records in column, code, last in column), printed by the generator in full
